meridianLog.note: Five rejected drafts of one bio before Eddie wrote a better version himself in ChatGPT. Root cause: transcribing his bullet facts into comma-lists instead of finding an idea that reorganizes them. Durable fix: craft gate added to the agent's self-check, plus 8 binding craft rules and a study of the lines of Eddie's that beat every agency draft.

Useful for finding blind spots (no photos, no capacity answer, caterers had no home on the page). But twice recommended adding content that already existed elsewhere on the same page, because it was handed a section with no page context. Rule added: review the whole page or the finding is invalid.

Caught three unsupported promises that would have shipped to the audience most likely to hold Eddie to them. Operations surfaced the Hope's Way contradiction nobody else did. The Giveaway Rule generalized correctly from money to capacity.

Ran Functional only on the first one-pager and reported a pass. Skipped the UX and Customer Mindset lenses entirely, so an overloaded hero and a 531-word flyer shipped to Eddie, who called it trash. All three lenses are mandatory, and Functional alone is never a pass.

meridianLog.subject: 513Sips Board
meridianLog.note: Board unanimously approved a $500 giveaway against a booking carrying $30 of margin. Rachel accepted Vivian's 'labor, not product' framing without pricing Eddie's hours — violating the Board's own written rule that the CFO always runs total engagement hours. Worst case was -$195 cash (vendor-backed picks) or 6-8 unpaid hours (labor-backed picks). Eddie caught it in one read and was rightly angry. Correct agent and correct framing (upgrade beats discount); indefensible sizing.
correctiveActions: Added 'The Giveaway Rule' to Board shared operational DNA — every prize/discount/trade must state cash-out-by-vendor and Eddie's hours at $75/hr against actual booking margin before a vote
Added affordability as item 7 of the Chief of Staff pre-adjourn checklist — 'buildable' is not 'affordable'
Refinement notes written for Rachel (primary miss), Vivian (framing), Danny (never valued what was given away), and Chief of Staff (executability != affordability)
meridianLog.resolution: Prize resized to $150 stated value — 513Sips home cocktail kit (~$25 cash, delivered unconditionally) plus a custom signature cocktail named for the winner ($125 stated, $0 cash, ~3 hrs prep, redeemable only on a booking of $650+). Hard rule adopted: nothing requiring a vendor payment may ever be giveaway currency.

tips.current: Your master backlog drifts from project backlogs between sessions — completed work stays open, new items go untracked.
tips.better: Open any session with: 'Act as Chief of Staff, run a backlog sync.' Takes 2 minutes and keeps the dashboard honest. Make it a habit before picking your next task.

tips.current: Leads go cold silently. No record of last contact, no way to know when to follow up.
tips.better: Communication Log is the highest-CEO-priority Books feature. Even a simple note field per lead gives you 80% of the value. Start there before building the full schema.

tips.better: After this session, pause and run Meridian scoring. Right agent (1-5), quality (1-5). If anything scores below 4, note the refinement. It takes 90 seconds and compounds over time.

tips.better: The first real engagement will reveal gaps no amount of planning uncovers. Pick any business you've noticed has a weak site. Run it through Engagement Manager. Outcome matters less than pipeline validation.

tips.better: Open with: 'Working on [X]. Last session: [Y]. Today: [Z]. Start with [first task].' Eliminates warm-up entirely — first pass is production-quality.

bestPractices.title: Chief of Staff as Session Opener
bestPractices.body: Before any work session, spend 2 minutes with Chief of Staff. Read the sync report. Know what's actually P1. Then open your working session with full context — no surprises mid-session.

bestPractices.title: Meridian Scoring Habit
bestPractices.body: At session end: Right agent (1-5)? Output quality (1-5)? If either < 4, one sentence on what to improve. Saves to vault. Feeds agent refinement over time. 90 seconds of investment per session.

bestPractices.title: Opus 4 vs Sonnet vs Haiku
bestPractices.body: Opus: Board reviews, pricing strategy, legal review, complex architecture. Sonnet: builds, saves, blog work, domain agents, design pipeline. Haiku: quick lookups, formatting, data transformation, routine logging.

bestPractices.title: Agent Prompt Structure
bestPractices.body: Best agents have: (1) Role + persona, (2) Scope boundaries — what they do AND don't, (3) Output format, (4) 2–3 example invocations. Skip any and outputs get inconsistent.

bestPractices.title: Session Handoff Value
bestPractices.body: Write handoffs as if a stranger is picking up tomorrow with no context. What do they absolutely need to know? Everything else is noise. The handoff is the session's entire lasting value.
